summary: This joint resolution terminates the national emergency declared by the President on July 30, 2025, in Executive Order 14323.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a joint resolution terminating a specific national emergency declared by executive order. It contains no provisions, authorizations, or references related to federal expenditures, appropriations, or budget authority. Therefore, it has no bearing on government spending.
The bill text addresses only the termination of a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act and makes no mention of tax policy, rates, credits, or revenue measures. No relation exists.
No provisions in the bill address healthcare policy, coverage, funding, or regulation. The measure is strictly procedural regarding an emergency declaration.
The bill does not reference firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues in any way.
While national emergencies can sometimes involve border policy, this resolution provides no details on the subject of the emergency and contains no immigration-related language or directives.
The bill has zero content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The resolution terminates an unspecified national emergency and is referred to the Foreign Affairs Committee, but it includes no language on defense spending, military operations, or authorizations.
No environmental, energy, or climate provisions appear in the bill text.
The bill does not engage with welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
No education policy, funding, or school-related measures are present.
The legislation contains nothing related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No provisions address policing, sentencing, incarceration, or justice reform.
The bill makes no reference to tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
While emergencies can indirectly affect deficits, this resolution offers no fiscal directives or debt-related language.
The bill does not address LGBTQ+ protections, rights, or related civil rights matters.
Although referred to the Foreign Affairs Committee, the text contains no provisions on foreign assistance, aid levels, or international programs.
No election administration, voting access, or electoral integrity measures are included.
The resolution has no content concerning technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance.
No labor, employment, or union-related provisions exist in the bill.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions, civil rights, or anti-discrimination policy.
